subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Friction in Extreme Environments
description: A fast breakdown of Friction in Extreme Environments for builders.

hook.text: In space there's no air. On Mars, dust is razor-sharp. Friction changes.

buildup.text: Extreme cold thickens lubricants. Extreme heat burns them off entirely.

discovery.text: Solid films, ceramics, and special alloys handle harsh conditions.

twist.text: In vacuum, metals cold-weld on contact. Lubrication is critical.

climax.text: Mars rovers use dry-film bearings designed to last a decade in dust.

punchline.text: Where oil can't go, clever engineering finds a way.

quiz.question: Why is lubrication in space uniquely hard?
options: Gravity is needed to keep oil in the bearing
Vacuum causes cold-welding and extremes ruin conventional lubricants
Cosmic radiation breaks down all lubricant molecules
